:::{#hero-heading}

::: {#professional-bio-panel}
I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics & Data Science at Oregon State University. My work thus far focuses on network analysis, causal inference and peer effects, which I mostly study using tools from multivariate statistics.

Previously, I was a Postdoctoral Scholar at Stanford University in the Economics Department, where I worked with [Arun Chandrasekhar](https://stanford.edu/~arungc/) on econometric methods for development economics. I completed my PhD in Statistics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where I was co-advised by [Keith Levin](https://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~kdlevin/) and [Karl Rohe](http://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~karlrohe/). During my PhD I spent some time working on [`broom`](https://broom.tidymodels.org/), a popular open-source `R` package in the `tidyverse`, and I interned at Posit (formerly RStudio) and Facebook. Before grad school, I studied statistics at Rice University.

I keep [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=6g1T3WIAAAAJ) up to date. My intermittently updated curriculum vitae is available [here](academic-cv.pdf).

[Click here for a non-academic bio.](#fun-bio){.bio-switch}
:::

::: {#fun-bio-panel}

In recent years I've enjoyed board games as a way to take my mind off work. Recent favorites include Root, which allows me to indulge my inner competitive streak, and also co-ops such as Spirit Island, which allows me to give myself a violent headache. I regularly host and attend large party games like Blood on the Clocktower, both for the thrill of finding hidden traitors and for the chance to meet lots of new people.

During my postdoc, I got back into being consistently active, and I put much of my open calendar towards weightlifting and group rides in the Santa Cruz mountains. I'm a big fan of playing recreational sports poorly. In Corvallis I'm excited to find pickup ultimate frisbee, pickleball partners, and fellow climbers; I'm pondering social dance as a next underdeveloped hobby. Together with some college friends, I'm learning about snow travel and mountaineering and we plan to explore some of the glaciated peaks in the PNW.

During my last year in Palo Alto, I picked up the guitar at a local music school, child prodigies hammering out Beethoven in the next room as I struggled through classics such as Twinkle Twinkle Little Star and Mary Had A Little Lamb. While I am not particularly artsy myself, I've recently enjoyed being dragged to arthouse movies, thrifting with friends who have better aesthetic sensibilities than me, and reading speculative fiction. Ursula K. Le Guin's Hainish Cycle is a favorite.

In Oregon, I'd like to put down roots after my recent transient year as a postdoc. I'd especially like to connect with other junior faculty, and I'm hoping to get back in the habit of hosting dinner parties on a regular basis.

[Back to the academic bio.](#professional-bio){.bio-switch}
:::

:::

I'm actively looking to for PhD students to work with. I'm also looking for collaborators across Oregon State, and especially collaborators within the College of Agriculture. Please reach out if you have statistics questions!

## recent news

- 2026-09-16: I joined Oregon State University as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics and Data Science.

- 2026-07-29: I presented at New Researchers Conference 2026 about some recent work on estimating peer effects in noisy networks [slide](https://github.com/alexpghayes/2026-09-nrc-lightning-talk)

- 2026-04-11: I presented on [Spectral Estimation and Trait Selection for Aggregated Relational Data](https://github.com/alexpghayes/2026-04-11-nsec-2026) at Network Science in Economics 2026.

- 2026-04-09: I have a new working paper [Estimating peer effects in noisy, low-rank networks via network smoothing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03204) with Keith Levin.

Material from older talks, presentations, posters, etc, can be found [on my Github](https://github.com/alexpghayes/).
